This integration drives your **Somfy RTS** shades and blinds through the
**Somfy MyLink bridge**, on your local network: open, close, stop, favourite
position ("my") and MyLink scenes. It talks to the "Synergy" API of the bridge
(TCP, port 44100); the Somfy cloud is not used.

> **Unofficial**, not affiliated with Somfy. The integration has **never been
> tested with a real bridge** yet: it follows the protocol of the
> pysomfymylink library (the one of Home Assistant). Your feedback is welcome.

## Before you start

1. Set up the bridge and your shades in the **MyLink** app.
2. In the app, menu **Integration**, note the **System ID**.
3. Give the bridge a fixed IP address in your router (DHCP reservation).

## Configuration

- **Address of the bridge**: its IP address, like `192.168.1.60` (port 44100
  by default; `192.168.1.60:44100` is accepted).
- **System ID**: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only
  to your bridge. It never appears in a log, a status or `/data`.
- **Read interval** (60 to 3600 s, 300 by default): the list of shades and
  scenes is read again at this pace, only to know whether the bridge answers.
- **Language** of the feature names.

The **Test the connection** button reads the bridge again (at most once a
minute).

## What you get

- A **shutter** per motor of the bridge: `Open / close` (open, close, stop)
  and a `Favourite position (my)` button.
- A **button** per MyLink scene (`Run`).

Never a switch: a "turn everything off" does not reach your shades.

## The state is assumed, never confirmed

RTS motors are **one-way**: they send back neither their state nor their
position, and the bridge only says it took the command. So:

- there is **no position** in Gladys;
- the value Gladys shows for `Open / close` is the **last command sent**, not
  a measured state: a shade shown "closed" was told to close, nothing more (a
  remote, an obstacle or the thermal protection of the motor may have changed
  it);
- the badge of each shade (orange dot) says "Assumed state" with the last
  command and whether the bridge accepted it;
- no command can be "confirmed by a read": a successful command means
  "accepted by the bridge" (it answered). Without an answer of the bridge,
  Gladys shows an error "sent, but the bridge did not answer: state unknown"
  (the command may have left: it is never told "not sent").

**Stop and favourite position**: on an RTS motor this is the same "my"
button. While moving, it stops the shade; at rest, it sends it to its
favourite position. The bridge does not know whether the shade moves: pressing
stop while the shade is still moves it to its favourite position.

## Stop and close

Stop and close go **before** the other commands: a read in progress is cut,
and they wait neither for the list of shades, nor for a System ID validated by
a read, nor for a recent read. The bridge accepts one connection, and the
integration sends it **one request at a time**, each after the answer of the
bridge to the previous one. When the request in flight has had no answer for a
second, the connection is cut, and the stop or close goes on a new connection
once the old one is closed. A Gladys scene on five shades therefore takes five
times the answer time of the bridge; what could not leave within 3.5 s is held
(see below).

**The newest wins, from its arrival**: any new click on a shade (open, close,
stop, favourite position), whether it leaves or not, cancels the held command
of that shade; running a MyLink scene cancels every held command.

They are refused (an error in Gladys) in these cases, and only these:

1. the address or the System ID is missing in the configuration, or the
   configuration could not be read from Gladys yet (nothing is sent);
2. the value received is not "close" or "stop";
3. a newer command of the same shade has already left;
4. the bridge answers an error or an unexpected answer (System ID refused,
   shade unknown to the bridge): the message says so;
5. **stop** written without an answer of the bridge: error "check the shade";
   it is **never sent again** (at rest, stop moves the shade to its favourite
   position);
6. **stop** not sent within 3.5 s (bridge not reachable, tries every 250 ms):
   it is held and tried again from 4 s, **never written later than 8 s after
   the click** (later, the shade has often finished its travel and the stop
   would move it to its favourite position);
7. **close** without an answer of the bridge within 3.5 s: it is written
   again on a new connection within that time, then held and tried again 5, 12
   and 25 s after the click (3 s each, until about 30 s).

A held command lives **in memory only**: if the integration restarts, it is
lost, never replayed; the badge of the shade then says "not sent or not
confirmed: check the shade".

## Open, favourite position, scenes

They are refused, nothing sent, when: the address or the System ID is missing
or the configuration is not read yet; the bridge refused the System ID; the
shade or scene is not in the list read from the bridge (Scan button of the
Discovery tab); 32 commands are already waiting; a newer stop or close of the
same shade (for a scene: of any shade) arrived before they left; they could not
leave within 3.5 s (bridge busy or not reachable). Written without an answer of
the bridge, they show an error "state unknown". They are never tried again.

## Direction of each shade

Check the direction of each shade before using it in a scene: on a motor
wired the other way round, "close" opens. Home Assistant has a "reverse"
option; it is planned here later.

## System ID refused

When the bridge refuses the System ID, the integration stops reading the
bridge (the refusal is kept in `/data` as an 8-bit marker that cannot give the
System ID back) until you save another System ID, **Test the connection**
succeeds, or the bridge answers a command without an error. Stop and close are
still sent.

## Privacy

Everything stays on your local network. `/data` holds the time of the last
read, the list of shades and scenes (ids and names), the last command of each
shade and the commands left "not sent" (for the badge, never sent again);
never the System ID.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Somfy MyLink asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Somfy RTS shades in Gladys | `section` | No | Each shade of your MyLink bridge becomes a shutter in the Discovery tab (open, close, stop, favourite position), and each MyLink scene a button. RTS motors never send their state back: Gladys only knows the last command sent, shown as an assumed state, never as a fact. Everything stays on your local network (the Synergy API of the bridge, port 44100). Never tested with a real bridge yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with Somfy. |
| Address of the bridge | `string` | Yes | The local IP address of your MyLink bridge, like 192.168.1.60. Give it a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation). |
| System ID | `secret` | Yes | Shown in the MyLink app, menu Integration. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to your bridge. |
| Read interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the list of shades and scenes is read from the bridge (60 to 3600 s). It only tells whether the bridge answers: RTS motors have no state to read. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the features of the devices added from now on. |

## How to install Somfy MyLink in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Somfy MyLink appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-somfy-mylink:0.1.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-somfy-mylink](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-somfy-mylink).

Somfy MyLink requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Somfy MyLink is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
